limitations: Tagging-stage component benchmark: production thumbnail regeneration/cache encoding, JPEG decoding, Core Image preprocessing, worker inference, vocabulary and probability encoding. It excludes interactive UI, session frame lookup/progress publication, video analysis/scoring/grouping and export.
Video-backed trials regenerate every requested thumbnail from a synthetic 1920x1080 H.264 clip. Benefit depends on cache misses, source codec, seek cost and machine load.
Cached trials create a 64-JPEG cache from the retained RGBA corpus before timing; their memory includes residual fixture-construction allocator pages. Compare memory within the same fixture mode.

Combined memory is the peak simultaneous sum of parent and direct-child physical footprints sampled via proc_pid_rusage every 10 ms. This is not unique DRAM use; shared mappings may be counted by both processes. OS codec/XPC service memory is excluded.
M4 starts require normal thermal state, GPU <=55 C, and sampled maximum P/E scaled CPU usage <=40%. Background macOS processes and clocks still vary.
Controls and candidates run in separate fresh processes. All 64 encoded outputs match by SHA256 across configurations within each input mode, and are byte-compared across repeated sweeps.

Prototype worker binaries enabled shared input by default; final code retains copy input by default and exposes the same shared implementation through --shared-input or WAIFU_WD_SHARED_INPUT=1. Benchmark scripts now request the experimental mode explicitly. Warmup/startup are excluded from timing.

Shared input saved about 6.5 MB in the M4 worker trials but did not establish a speed gain and did not reproduce a consistent memory benefit in an earlier M3 trial; it remains experimental. No further M3 tests were run after the user requested M4-only testing.

An initial app sampler run was discarded after correcting the child-PID count interpretation. Only corrected runs are included here. The corrected sampler also rejects runs that never observe worker memory.
Model-only Core ML comparisons remain those in WDTagger-native-m4.md; this pass does not measure a new model-only speed advantage over Core ML. No additional GPU trace was recorded.
